subject: Sizing Ask: tailored GPU tranche & conditional discount for Verde Health
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@verdehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing Ask: tailored GPU tranche & conditional discount for Verde Health

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I pulled together an initial sizing recommendation for the Reserved capacity tranche Verde Health mentioned during discovery. High level:

- Proposed committed tranche: 120 A100-equivalent GPU-hours per month (phased onboarding over 6 weeks).
- Short-term burst allowance: +25% monthly burst pool to handle clinical peak windows (billed at burst rate).
- Suggested term: 6 months with a renewal review tied to throughput and model efficiency improvements.

One ask from your procurement thread was to include pricing safeguards tied to upstream GPU cost movement. We can offer a conditional credit structure that triggers if the market GPU-index (third-party GPU index we both referenced) increases beyond agreed thresholds during the term. I sketched the idea below and attached your RFP so we can reference target workloads.

Why this structure helps Verde Health: predictable committed capacity for near-term ramp, while sharing some risk if GPU costs materially spike. Why it helps Redwood: preserves committed revenue while keeping approval overhead lower than blanket discounts.

Next steps: can you confirm the expected steady-state monthly inference hours (or send a 2-week sample of token/hour curves) so we can finalize the tranche sizing? If procurement wants a draft clause, I can circulate a short conditional-credit language for legal review — looped in Karthik and Ben.

Attaching: VerdeHealth_RFP.pdf

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@verdehealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing Ask: tailored GPU tranche & conditional discount for Verde Health

Camila —

Appreciate the quick follow. Verde Health is comfortable with the proposed tranche shape in principle; before we move to contract language procurement has two asks:

1) Formalize the price-sensitivity mechanism. We prefer a "price collar" style clause rather than a one-off credit: if the agreed industry GPU index (we'll propose SP-GPU-Index) increases more than 12% vs the baseline quarter, Redwood would issue a monthly credit equal to X% of overage charges (or a fixed $/GPU-hour credit). If index decreases, pricing remains as quoted.

2) Approval thresholds — procurement cannot accept open-ended discounts. We need an explicit upper bound on cumulative credits over the 6-month term (either % of committed spend or $ cap).

Can you have your finance/legal provide draft language and an example sensitivity table showing the impact on monthly unit economics for +10%, +20%, +30% index moves? Also include who in Redwood signs off on >10% cumulative credit exposure.

Thanks — looping in procurement for visibility.

Best,
Asha Kapoor
Head of Partnerships (acting)
Verde Health
asha.kapoor@verdehealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-26T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing Ask: tailored GPU tranche & conditional discount for Verde Health

Camila / Ben —

Quick notes on procurement's asks and our internal approval path. I ran a quick sensitivity against our cost model (attached). Key points:

- Baseline unit cost assumptions used: $2.75 / A100-equivalent gpu-hour (internal blended run-rate).
- Proposed consumer-facing committed price: $3.50 / gpu-hour (reflects committed discount and reserved capacity uplift).

Conditional credit framing options (recommended):
A) Tiered credit by index move: 12–20% index increase -> 7% monthly credit on overage; 20–35% -> 12% monthly credit; >35% -> cap at 18% and executive approval required.
B) Dollar cap alternative: credits capped at 15% of committed monthly spend (simpler for procurement).

Approval requirements: up to 10% cumulative credit across term — sales director OK. 10–18% requires VP sales + finance concurrence. >18% requires CRO + finance exec signoff.

Trade-offs: A) is more customer-friendly and transparent for large swings, B) is easier to model and more protective for us. For Verde Health (mid-market with variable burst patterns) I recommend A) with a hard dollar cap equal to 15% of committed monthly spend to satisfy procurement. That keeps the clause readable and limits our downside predictably.

I've attached a modeled spreadsheet (pricing-model-verde.xlsx) with +10/+20/+30% scenarios. Ben — can you double-check whether we have the runway to approve tier A1 (7%) at the AE/Director level? If not, we'll need to fast-track a short exec approval note.

-Karthik
Director, Deal Structuring
Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@verdehealth.com>, procurement@verdehealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing Ask: tailored GPU tranche & conditional discount for Verde Health

Asha / procurement team —

Thanks for the clarity and for surfacing the approval constraints. Based on our internal review we can commit to the following, which balances Verde Health's desire for protection with Redwood's need for predictable committed economics:

Summary proposal (6-month term, 120 A100-equivalent GPU-hours/month committed tranche):
- Base committed price: $3.50 / GPU-hour (as quoted).
- Conditional Price Collar & Credits:
  * If SP-GPU-Index increases 12–20% vs baseline quarter: 7% credit applied to overage charges for that month.
  * If increase 20–35%: 12% credit applied to overage charges for that month.
  * If increase >35%: 18% credit applied, subject to executive review (CRO + Finance).
- Hard cap: total monthly credits cannot exceed 15% of committed monthly spend (this protects both parties from runaway liability).
- Reporting: We will publish monthly index reconciliations and a one-line credit calculation in the invoice.

Attached is a short draft clause (proposed-conditional-clause.docx) and a link to the HubSpot deal (for internal tracking). If this structure is acceptable, I will:
1) Share a redline-ready SOW with the clause inserted for your legal/procurement.
2) Spin up the DocuSign skeleton so procurement can review signature workflow.
3) Schedule a 30-minute wrap call to align on onboarding and telemetry to measure actual hours.

Would you be available for a call on Monday morning PT?

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive
